turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_retention_train.csv: 55 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S) and `target` (the measured hot-strength retention ratio
    YS(600C)/YS(20C)).
  - b3_htsteel_retention_pool.csv: 26 CANDIDATE samples whose hot-strength
    retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C) was NOT measured, columns
    `candidate_id` and the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST hot-
strength retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C), then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set shows that the highest retention values arise from two distinct composition families (plus one isolated low-alloy point):

- Ni-base / high-Ni Fe-base alloys containing substantial W + Ti + Al (targets 1.00, 0.875, 0.821, 0.903).  
- The single low-alloy heat 0.5Cr-0.5Mo (target 0.9375).  
- High-Mn + high-V austenitics (targets 0.88–0.80) that have no close analogues in the pool.

Nearest-neighbour matching of the 26 candidates against these families immediately isolates five compositions:

- c019 is essentially the 36Ni-3W-Ti alloy that recorded 1.00 (only Ti and Al are higher).  
- c015 is compositionally almost identical to the 0.9375 low-alloy point.  
- c011 reproduces the high-Ti, ~20Ni, Al-bearing analysis that recorded 0.903.  
- c013 and c004 are the 27Ni-Ti-Al-(Mo/W) variants that recorded 0.821.

All remaining candidates lie near training points whose targets are \(\le 0.77\).  Ranking the five by the training targets of their nearest neighbours (and by the extra strengthening elements present) therefore yields

Final: c019, c015, c011, c013, c004
